title: Interactive element without a meaningful name
user_impact: Screen reader users are not told what the element does.
technical_impact: An element whose role requires a name (such as checkbox, combobox, listbox, radio, slider, switch, tab, textbox, menu item, image role, or a form field whose label is empty) has no accessible name from aria-label, aria-labelledby, a label or its content, so a screen reader announces only the role; buttons, links, dialogs, <summary> and fields without any label have their own rules.

checks.source: WCAG 2.2 SC 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value; WAI-ARIA 1.2 (Accessible Name Required: True); accname 1.2
checks.applicability: Elements in the accessibility tree whose role requires a name (checkbox, combobox, listbox, menuitem*, meter, option, progressbar, radio, radiogroup, searchbox, slider, spinbutton, switch, tab, textbox, tree, treeitem, ...), except a[href] (links/name-missing), buttons (buttons/name-missing), dialogs (dialog/name-missing) and native fields with no label source at all (forms/label-missing).
checks.expectation:
Fails when the computed name is empty: a custom slider without label, a switch whose
aria-labelledby points at empty text, a native field whose <label> is blank, a listbox or tree
without name. Every name source passes: aria-label, aria-labelledby, <label>, title on a native
field, content for name-from-content roles. Hidden subtrees are out of scope.
